issue.unclosed_block: Block “{key}” is never closed: a “}}” is missing.
issue.unexpected_close_brace: Stray “}}”: there is no open block.
issue.unterminated_string: A string is not closed: the closing quote is missing.
issue.invalid_key: A block cannot be used as a key.
issue.multiline_string: A string spans several lines: is a quote missing?
issue.control_character: The file has invisible control characters.
issue.invisible_character: A word has an invisible character.

issue.stray_bom: The file starts with a UTF-8 BOM that the game glues to the first key.

issue.duplicate_key: Key “{key}” is repeated: the game uses the first one.

issue.semicolon_in_quotes: A text of row “{key}” has a “;” inside quotes: it shifts the columns.
issue.unencodable_character: A character cannot be saved in the file's encoding.
issue.header_row: Header row: the game loads it as one more entry.
issue.read_error: The file could not be read.
issue.mod_shadow_identical: “{rel}” is identical to the game's (or a dependency's): the mod's copy changes nothing.
issue.case_collision: “{rel}” and “{other}” only differ in case: Windows will mix them up.
issue.windows_reserved_name: Windows does not accept “{folder}” as a name (CON, NUL, COM1…, the characters <>:"|?* or a trailing dot or space).

issue.descriptor_other_folder: “path” points to the folder “{folder}”, but the mod is in “{actual}”: the game will not find it.
issue.descriptor_missing_folder: “path” points to “{path}”, which does not exist in the game folder.
issue.descriptor_bad_user_dir: “user_dir” must be a valid Windows folder name: "{user_dir}".
issue.descriptor_bad_replace_path: “replace_path” must be a folder relative to the game folder, without “..” or a drive: "{replace_path}".
issue.descriptor_user_dir_empty: Without “user_dir”, the mod's saved games and cache are stored with those of the base game.
issue.replace_path_empty: “replace_path” hides the base game's “{replace_path}” folder, but the mod has no files in it: the game will be left without those files.
issue.replace_path_hides_referenced: “replace_path” hides “{replace_path}”, but {count} references still name files of that folder that the mod does not have (e.g. in {example}).

issue.tag_invalid: “{tag}” is not a valid TAG: three uppercase letters or digits starting with a letter, not a script word or a reserved Windows name.

issue.country_file_missing: The country file “{file}” of {tag} does not exist.

issue.nationalvalue_unknown: National value “{name}” does not exist (the game only defines those of common/nationalvalues.txt).
issue.reform_unknown: “{group} = {name}” is not a reform: the group or the option does not exist in common/issues.txt.

issue.bmp_color_unmapped: Colour {color} of the province map ({pixels} pixels) has no row with an id in definition.csv.

explain.outcome.unclosed_block: The game will misread everything after the missing brace.
explain.outcome.unexpected_close_brace: The game closes the outer block early there: what follows may end up outside the block it belongs to.
explain.title.missing_value: Why: The value of “{key}” is missing
explain.outcome.missing_value: The game has no value for “{key}”: it ignores the line or takes whatever comes next as its value.
explain.title.missing_key: Why: An operator has no key
explain.outcome.missing_key: The game does not know what that value belongs to: it drops it, and may misread what follows.
explain.title.unterminated_string: Why: A string is not closed
explain.outcome.unterminated_string: The game reads everything up to the next quote as text, even if it is several lines below.
explain.title.invalid_key: Why: A block cannot be used as a key
explain.outcome.invalid_key: The game does not accept a block as a key: it drops that assignment.
explain.outcome.unexpected_operator: The game does not expect that operator there: it may misread “{key}” and what follows.
explain.outcome.invalid_character: The game does not know what to do with that character: it may cut the word or the line there.
explain.title.multiline_string: Why: A string spans several lines
explain.outcome.multiline_string: If the quote is missing, the game joins several lines into one text and skips the keys caught inside.
explain.title.control_character: Why: The file has invisible control characters
explain.outcome.control_character: Those characters do not show in an editor, but the game reads them as part of the key or the text.
explain.title.invisible_character: Why: A word has an invisible character
explain.outcome.invisible_character: The word looks right, but to the game it is a different one: it does not match the key or id it looks for.
explain.title.non_game_encoding: Why: The file is not in Windows-1252
explain.outcome.non_game_encoding: The game reads the file as Windows-1252 and non-ASCII letters will look garbled.
explain.title.unreadable_encoding: Why: The file is in UTF-16
explain.outcome.unreadable_encoding: The game cannot read this file at all.
explain.title.stray_bom: Why: The file starts with a UTF-8 BOM that the game glues to the first key
explain.outcome.stray_bom: The game glues those bytes to the first key of the file: that key is not recognised.
explain.title.suspicious_close_brace: Why: A “}}” is less indented than expected
explain.outcome.suspicious_close_brace: If a “}}” really is missing before it, the game puts everything that follows into the wrong block.
explain.title.missing_end_marker: Why: Row “{key}” has no end marker “x”
explain.outcome.missing_end_marker: The game reads the row anyway: the final “x” is only the convention of the vanilla files.
explain.title.too_few_columns: Why: Row “{key}” is missing language columns
explain.outcome.too_few_columns: In the missing languages, the game has no text to show for “{key}”.
explain.outcome.duplicate_key: The game uses the first row with “{key}”: the others will never be seen.
explain.outcome.empty_key: Nothing can look up a row without a key: the game loads it, but it is never used.
explain.title.key_whitespace: Why: Key “{key}” has leading or trailing spaces
explain.outcome.key_whitespace: The game compares the key with its spaces: “{key}” will not match the key it looks for.
explain.title.semicolon_in_quotes: Why: A text of row “{key}” has a “;” inside quotes
explain.outcome.semicolon_in_quotes: The game does not understand quotes: it cuts the text at the “;” and the following languages shift one column.
explain.title.unencodable_character: Why: A character cannot be saved in the file's encoding
explain.outcome.unencodable_character: That character does not fit the file's encoding: change it, or convert the file, before saving.
explain.outcome.header_row: It is harmless: the game gets one extra entry with the header's key, which nothing uses.
explain.title.read_error: Why: The file could not be read
explain.outcome.read_error: The Studio could not check the file; if the problem is in the file, the game will not read it either.
explain.outcome.check_failed: It is a Studio failure, not the mod's: that check did not finish and its problems are missing from the list.
explain.title.mod_shadow_identical: Why this copy is not needed
explain.outcome.mod_shadow_identical: The game loads the mod's copy, but it is the same as the one it would load without it (the game's or a dependency's): deleting it changes nothing and makes the mod smaller.
explain.title.case_collision: Why: “{rel}” and “{other}” only differ in case
explain.outcome.case_collision: On Windows they cannot coexist: when the mod is copied or unzipped, one of them overwrites the other.
explain.title.windows_reserved_name: Why: Windows does not accept “{folder}” as a name (CON, NUL, COM1…, the characters <>
explain.outcome.windows_reserved_name: On Windows that file cannot be created or copied: the mod will arrive incomplete for whoever installs it.
explain.title.path_too_long: Why: The path of “{rel}” is {length} characters long
explain.outcome.path_too_long: On Windows, a path that long may fail when copying or loading: the game would not see the file.
explain.outcome.descriptor_no_name: The launcher has no name to show for the mod.
explain.outcome.descriptor_no_path: Without “path”, the game does not know which folder to load: the mod's files are not used.
explain.outcome.descriptor_bad_path: The game looks for the mod folder at “{path}”: it will not load its files.
explain.title.descriptor_other_folder: Why: “path” points to the folder “{folder}”, but the mod is in “{actual}”
explain.outcome.descriptor_other_folder: The game will load “{folder}”, not this folder: the changes made here will not show.
explain.title.descriptor_missing_folder: Why: “path” points to “{path}”, which does not exist in the game folder
explain.outcome.descriptor_missing_folde: The game does not find “{path}”: the mod loads no files.
explain.title.descriptor_bad_user_dir: Why: “user_dir” must be a valid Windows folder name
explain.outcome.descriptor_bad_user_dir: The game will not be able to create the mod's save folder with that name.
explain.title.descriptor_bad_replace_pat: Why: “replace_path” must be a folder relative to the game folder, without “..” or a drive
explain.outcome.descriptor_bad_replace_p: The game cannot apply that “replace_path”: it will not hide the folder you expect.
explain.title.descriptor_user_dir_empty: Why: Without “user_dir”, the mod's saved games and cache are stored with those of the base game
explain.outcome.descriptor_user_dir_empt: The mod's saves and the base game's are stored together and can get mixed up.
explain.outcome.replace_path_empty: The game will not load any file of “{replace_path}”: neither the base game's nor (since there are none) the mod's.
explain.outcome.replace_path_hides_refer: What is named inside “{replace_path}” will not be found in game.
explain.title.tag_not_registered: Why country {tag} does not exist in the game
explain.outcome.tag_not_registered: In game {tag} will not exist: the game does not load its history or its country file, and the provinces that name it as owner or core ({provinces}) point to a country that is not there.
explain.outcome.tag_not_registered_no_pr: In game {tag} will not exist: the game does not load its history or its country file, and whatever uses it points to a country that is not there.
explain.title.flag_tag_not_registered: Why nobody will see the flags of {tag}
explain.outcome.flag_tag_not_registered: The game only uses the flags of registered countries. If {tag} is a half-made country, it still needs its registration, its country file and its history; if it is left over, its flags can be deleted.
explain.title.tag_after_dynamic_tags: Why {tag} would be a dynamic dominion
explain.outcome.tag_after_dynamic_tags: The game will treat {tag} as a dynamic dominion (D01–D50): it will not be a playable country from the start.
explain.title.tag_invalid: Why: “{tag}” is not a valid TAG
explain.outcome.tag_invalid: The game does not accept “{tag}” as a country: it will not load, and whatever names it points to nothing.
explain.outcome.tag_taken: The game uses the first registration of {tag}; the second one is redundant.
explain.title.country_file_missing: Why: The country file “{file}” of {tag} does not exist
explain.outcome.country_file_missing: The game does not find {tag}'s country file: that country is not loaded and the game may close at startup.
explain.title.country_history_missing: Why: {tag} has no history in history/countries
explain.outcome.country_history_missing: {tag} will start the game without its own capital, culture or government, with whatever the game defaults to.
explain.outcome.country_history_duplicat: Two files give history to the same country; the game will use only one.
explain.outcome.ruling_party_not_of_coun: The game will not find {party} among the parties of {tag} and the country will start without a ruling party.
explain.title.ruling_party_ideology_not_: Why the government of {tag} does not allow {party}
explain.outcome.ruling_party_ideology_no: At the first election or reform the game will replace the ruling party of {tag}.
explain.title.party_unknown_policy: Why: Party {party} uses “{policy} = {value}”, which is not among the party issues of common/issues.txt
explain.outcome.party_unknown_policy: The game ignores “{policy}”: party {party} will not have that policy.
explain.title.government_missing_in_rebe: Why: Government {government} is not in the “government” table of the {rebel} rebels
explain.outcome.government_missing_in_re: If {rebel} rebels win in a country with {government}, the game does not know which government to switch to.
explain.title.government_election_withou: Why: Government {government} has “election = yes” but no “duration”
explain.outcome.government_election_with: The game will not know how often to call elections in {government}.
explain.title.upper_house_sum: Why: The upper house of {tag} adds up to {total}, not 100
explain.outcome.upper_house_sum: The game expects {tag}'s upper house to add up to 100: with {total}, the split will not be the one you wrote.
explain.title.duplicate_field: Why: “{name}” is repeated in the same block of the history of {tag} (first on line {first_line})
explain.outcome.duplicate_field: The game uses one of the two values of “{name}”; the other one is redundant.

explain.outcome.oob_file_missing: The country will start without the units of “{file}”.
explain.outcome.province_history_duplica: Two files give history to the same province; which one the game loads has not been checked in game.
explain.title.province_id_invalid: Why: Province {province} does not satisfy 1 ≤ id < {max} (max_provinces of default.map)
explain.outcome.province_id_invalid: The game does not load province {province}: its history and whatever names it are useless.
explain.title.bmp_color_unmapped: Why: Colour {color} of the province map ({pixels} pixels) has no row with an id in definition.csv
explain.outcome.bmp_color_unmapped: Those pixels belong to no province in game.
explain.title.land_province_without_regi: Why: Land province {province} is not in any state of region.txt
explain.outcome.land_province_without_re: A land province without a state cannot be managed in game, and the game may fail when loading it.
explain.title.land_province_multiple_reg: Why: Province {province} is in several states
explain.outcome.land_province_multiple_r: The game only puts province {province} in one of those states ({regions}): the others will not have it.
explain.title.sea_in_region: Why: Sea province {province} is in the state {region}
explain.outcome.sea_in_region: A sea province inside a state confuses the game: it may fail when loading or when working out {region}.
explain.title.land_province_without_cont: Why: Land province {province} is not on any continent
explain.outcome.land_province_without_co: Without a continent, province {province} does not get the continent modifiers the game would apply.
explain.title.loc_copy_degraded: Why the mod's “{file}” breaks game texts
explain.outcome.loc_copy_degraded: In game you will see “{example}” in {language} instead of “{original}”, because your {file} replaces the game's entirely.
explain.outcome.loc_key_missing: In game you will see the key “{key}” instead of the text.
explain.outcome.loc_untranslated: Players using {languages} will see no text for “{key}”.
explain.title.loc_key_orphan: Why: Nothing uses the mod's text “{key}”
explain.outcome.loc_key_orphan: It does no harm: the game loads “{key}”, but nothing shows it. It may be a leftover, or a typo in the key that uses it.
explain.outcome.event_id_duplicate: Two events with the same id: the game will only use one and the other will never fire.
explain.title.event_id_invalid: Why: Event id {event} is out of the range the game accepts
explain.outcome.event_id_invalid: The game does not handle an event with id {event} well: it may never fire or be confused with another.
explain.title.event_ref_missing: Why: Event {event} is fired, but it does not exist
explain.outcome.event_ref_missing: When fired, event {event} will do nothing (it does not exist).
explain.outcome.decision_duplicate: Two decisions with the same name: the game will only show one.
explain.outcome.decision_picture_missing: Decision {decision} still works, but it shows without its picture.
explain.title.cb_not_in_peace_order: Why: Casus belli {cb} is not in “peace_order”
explain.outcome.cb_not_in_peace_order: When negotiating peace, the game does not know where to place {cb}: it may not be offered.
explain.title.peace_order_unknown: Why: “{cb}” is in “peace_order” but it is not a casus belli
explain.outcome.peace_order_unknown: The game ignores “{cb}” in the peace order.
explain.outcome.generic: The game loads the winning layer; the others do not count.

fix_error.not_applicable: This fix does not apply to this problem.

fix_error.no_game_file: “{file}” has no game file to restore the rows from.
